title: Affinity hints and probe heuristics — inventory notes (WIP)
content:
Context: working notes on how the control plane should surface lightweight affinity hints and health probes for routing decisions across regions. Focus is on minimizing false negatives (avoiding healthy GPUs being excluded) while ensuring quick detection of real degradation that should change routing decisions. This is 'inventory-first' thinking: treat the catalog as an authoritative, eventually-consistent ledger with probes that annotate state rather than try to be the single source of truth for live decisions.

Goals and constraints:
- Low-cost probes: avoid expensive full-model warmups. Prefer telemetry + micro-probes.
- Deterministic routing hints: concise label set that routing layer can evaluate quickly (<=2 label checks per request).
- Multi-region safety: prefer local region unless routing hint indicates insufficient capacity or degraded GPUs.
- Fast failover: degrade to compatible model variants or fallback region within 200ms for latency-insensitive flows.

Label schema (proposal): (short, machine-friendly keys)
- infra.gpu.vendor = nvidia | amd | unknown
- infra.gpu.model = a100-80g | a100-40g | h100-80g | h100-40g | t4 | gtx | other
- infra.gpu.mig_count = "0|1|2|..." (string to keep flat schema)
- infra.gpu.mig_config = "mig:7g.20gb;..." (compact token for quick parsing)
- infra.gpu.compute_capability = "8.0"
- infra.gpu.driver = "535.86"
- infra.gpu.features = "tensor,fp16,kvcache-friendly" (comma list)
- infra.gpu.affinity = exclusive | shared | mixed (affinity hint for scheduling)
- infra.node.region = us-west1 | eu-central1 | ap-northeast1
- infra.node.az = us-west1-a
- infra.node.pool = gpu-dedicated | gpu-spot | mixed
- infra.health.last_heartbeat = <RFC3339 timestamp>
- infra.health.load_1m = "0.6" (normalized to [0..1])
- infra.health.gpu_temp = "78C" (raw string; parser normalizes)
- infra.telemetry.kvcache_hit = "0.93" (0..1)
- infra.health.signal_score = "0..100" (computed by reconciler)

Health scoring (reconciler logic sketch):
- Sources: heartbeat, driver/daemon status, telemetry (kvcache hit, avg latency), probe microbench (single-batch latency), error rates from recent 5m window.
- Canonical score formula (tunable weights):
  base = 100
  subtract if: missing heartbeat > 30s -> -90
  driver mismatch or absent -> -60
  consecutive probe failures (>=3 in 5m) -> -50
  kvcache_hit_rate < 0.5 -> -(50*(0.5 - hit_rate))
  avg_infer_latency normalized vs profile -> scaled penalty
  final score = clamp(base - penalties, 0, 100)
- States derived from score:
  90-100: healthy
  60-89: degraded (soft-fallback allowed)
  30-59: unhealthy (prefer fallback variants / other regions)
  0-29: drain and quarantine

Probe heuristics (micro-probe design):
- Lightweight local probe: single-token generation with tiny model shard or dedicated probe binary that exercises attention + KV cache path. Not a full model run. Target <50ms on healthy GPU.
- Telemetry-driven probe triggers: if kvcache_hit drops by >15% compared to 1h baseline OR tail latency > 2x P50, schedule probe immediately.
- Probe backoff: exponential with jitter, but if probe fails 3x -> mark degraded and start drain procedures.
- Probe safety: probes must be able to be throttled cluster-wide to avoid amplification during incidents.

Reconciliation model and event flow:
- Node agent pushes heartbeat + local labels every 15s. Reconciler pulls extra telemetry (sinks: prometheus, pushgateway).
- Inventory ledger is append-only events + latest snapshot per node for quick reads. Use sequence numbers to avoid stale write wins.
- Reconciler writes computed infra.health.signal_score and infra.health.last_computed to catalog as annotations (not override agent labels).
- Conflict resolution: agent label wins for low-level inventory (driver version, MIG count). Reconciler annotations are authoritative for derived state (signal_score, derived_affinity).

Routing hints and policies (runtime interpretation):
- Only consider nodes with infra.health.signal_score >= 60 for latency-sensitive routes.
- For affinity-aware routes (large-batch or long-context): prefer infra.gpu.affinity=exclusive and infra.gpu.mig_count=0 or large-slice configs.
- For high-concurrency, small-context inference: prefer shared or mixed affinity and nodes with high kvcache_hit rates.
- Region preference: route to same region if at least 20% of capacity in that region is healthy for requested model profile. Else, consult fallback regions ordered by latency/commit tiers.
- Fallback mapping: maintain per-model compatibility table (model -> compatible GPU classes). If requested model not compatible with local GPUs, return a soft 409 with recommended route or trigger cross-region routing.

Operational playbook snippets (quick):
- If a region sees sudden drop in signal_score across many nodes: check driver rollout (recent package push), kernel logs, and telemetry spike; open P0 and start circuit-breaker.
- For noisy probes causing churn: increase probe success threshold from 3->5, apply hysteresis on state transitions for 10m.

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs):
- How to encode per-model runtime memory footprints into label space without exploding label cardinality? (Consider "model_profile" ids referenced by routing layer)
- Should reconciler annotate historical degradation windows to assist ML for predictive failovers? (practical but adds storage)
- How to securely surface driver mismatches for customers without leaking infra metadata? (need gating + redaction rules)
- Handling MIG dynamic reconfig (hot reconfigure) events: immediate label update vs scheduled drain?

References / links inside content:
- Jira: PLAT-452 (inventory event ledger work)
- PR: infra/#889 (reconciler annotations)
- Slack: #platform-node-inventory (thread 167834)

Immediate next steps (short list):
- Lock label key names and a first-cut compact encoding for mig_config (Marco take)
- Implement probe micro-binary prototype and measure 95th pctl on a100/h100 (Devon take)
- Add signal_score field to inventory snapshot schema and wire into routing alpha (Evelyn take)

Notes to reviewer: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and assumes we will iterate on weights and thresholds after measuring live signals. Looking for feedback on: label cardinality concerns, probe safety, and whether reconciler should push derived affinity vs routing layer deriving it on read.

Unresolved: should we include a per-node "trusted" boolean set by ops for emergency overrides? Pros: quick manual isolation. Cons: another cross-cutting flag that can complicate auto-scaling decisions.

Quick diff vs existing inventory: aim here to push derived lightweight hints (affinity, signal_score) into the catalog as annotations while retaining agent-authored low-level labels. This keeps the routing layer simple: read a few keys, apply policies, and route.

End of notes.
